answer: Agents earn standing only after their claims survive random audits backed by a bond: each agent locks scarce tokens, and an auditor who proves a claim false can slash that bond. The audit samples claims across accounts, so splitting one operator into many identities does not multiply the chance of passing; it multiplies the bonds at risk. A prism, lantern, or pigment can label an account, but none substitutes for locked value. The attacker must fund every identity and loses tokens when caught.
